title: Episode protocol, paired-outcome, and selection audit
purpose: Expose how task population, success definition, denominator, checkpoint selection, paired joint outcomes, cluster weighting, zero observed events, and pseudoreplicated exposures change reported policy evidence, while preserving uncertainty assumptions and separating distinct estimands from protocol diagnostics.
allowed_claims: The four authored protocols produce different success rates from the fixed episode table.
The protocol audit identifies task-population, success-definition, and denominator differences.
Wilson intervals communicate small-sample uncertainty under an independent Bernoulli interpretation.
The fixture keeps a valid timeout in the denominator and blocks aggregation when a technical-invalid attempt is declared.
The two-by-two protocol grid exposes a population-by-success-rule interaction on the authored rows.
A paired route-level fixture separates episode-micro and equal-route-macro estimands and enumerates its tiny cluster-bootstrap distribution.
Zero observed events retain a positive one-sided exact binomial upper bound under an explicit independent Bernoulli interpretation.
Repeating members within fixed route clusters does not create independent routes; per-episode event probability and per-new-route event incidence are distinct authored estimands.
The authored negative control distinguishes selection, final, and untouched confirmation roles and exposes a 0.25 reuse gap when the final column is improperly used to choose a checkpoint.
Two paired tables can share candidate and baseline marginal success rates and the same point difference while having different discordant cells and exact conditional McNemar diagnostics.
forbidden_claims: The fixture estimates performance of a policy, simulator, robot, or autonomous vehicle.
Wilson intervals make results from different protocols directly comparable.
Zero observed collisions or interventions implies zero deployment risk.
Four authored route clusters provide a calibrated population confidence interval or prove that the candidate policy is equivalent to the baseline.
The cluster-incidence upper bound is a corrected estimate of the same per-episode probability, or either authored bound estimates real vehicle risk.
The authored checkpoint table estimates expected selection bias, proves checkpoint-d is worse, or measures model generalization.
The paired-margin p-values prove a policy effect, equivalence, cluster independence, multiplicity control, or deployment safety.

systems.name: fixed_episode_table
systems.type: hand-authored table of eight completed episode outcomes
systems.preprocessing: select episodes by named suite; validate end semantics; do not delete failed, truncated, safety-violating, or declared-invalid rows

systems.name: paired_route_table
systems.type: hand-authored table of ten paired outcomes nested in four routes
systems.preprocessing: validate unique pairs; compute candidate-minus-baseline within each pair; average within route before resampling routes with replacement

systems.name: analytic_zero_event_calculator
systems.type: exact standard-library one-sided binomial bound calculator
inputs: declared independent exposure or cluster count
outputs: episode-iid versus cluster-incidence pseudoreplication audit with explicit estimand labels
systems.preprocessing: solve (1-p_upper)^n = alpha directly for the declared unit; never relabel repeated cluster members as independent routes or treat the episode and cluster bounds as one parameter

systems.name: checkpoint_selection_table
systems.type: hand-authored table of four checkpoints with three score roles
outputs: final-reuse-chosen checkpoint, reused score, confirmation score, and authored reuse gap
systems.preprocessing: validate unique checkpoints and finite [0,1] scores; reject tied selection or final maxima; select once on the selection column, then contrast with the invalid final-column reuse path

systems.name: paired_margin_tables
systems.type: two hand-authored twenty-pair binary joint tables with fixed margins
outputs: equal-tail exact conditional two-sided McNemar p-value
systems.preprocessing: validate unique pair identities and Boolean outcomes; preserve all four joint cells; condition only on the observed discordant count under the named symmetric null

datasets.name: procedural eight-episode factorial evaluation table with explicit end semantics
datasets.split_definition: Four easy and four hard authored attempts crossed with goal-only and safety-aware success rules; hard-2 is a valid timeout truncation.
datasets.unit_of_analysis: attempted episode with explicit validity and end flags
leakage_controls: Episode outcomes are immutable inputs rather than fitted observations.
The full protocol retains all eight episode rows, including the valid timeout failure.
A declared technical-invalid attempt blocks aggregation instead of being filtered after outcomes are known.
All four population-by-success-rule cells are reported before interpreting the endpoint difference.
Protocol diagnostics are not presented as independent causal contributions.

datasets.name: procedural ten-pair route-cluster comparison table
datasets.split_definition: Ten immutable candidate-baseline pairs: four on route-a, four on route-b, one on route-c, and one on route-d.
datasets.unit_of_analysis: paired policy outcome nested in a route cluster; the target macro estimand gives each route equal weight
leakage_controls: Candidate and baseline outcomes remain paired under the same route and pair identity.
Route means are computed before cluster resampling, so extra repeats do not silently redefine the macro estimand.
All four observed route clusters are enumerated with replacement for the deterministic teaching distribution.
The four-cluster percentile interval is explicitly barred from population calibration claims.

datasets.name: procedural zero-event route-replay pseudoreplication table
datasets.split_definition: Ten authored route identities with ten zero-event repeated members per route; a one-repeat negative control preserves the same route identities.
datasets.unit_of_analysis: declared independently sampled episode for one estimand or route cluster with any-event outcome for the other; the two parameters remain separate
leakage_controls: Repeats never create new route identities.
Episode-event and new-route-incidence bounds retain distinct names and interpretations.
Changing repeats per route cannot change the independent route count.
Changing repeats per route changes the any-event cluster outcome even when the bound formula has the same numeric input count.
Neither authored count is presented as observed simulator, robot, vehicle, or population exposure.

datasets.name: procedural four-checkpoint three-split score table
datasets.split_definition: Four authored checkpoint identities each have distinct selection, final, and untouched confirmation score roles.
datasets.unit_of_analysis: checkpoint score record; no score is an observed model result
leakage_controls: The legitimate path chooses exactly once using only the selection column.
The final column is reported only after that choice and is not fed back into selection.
The negative control deliberately violates the role boundary by maximizing the final column.
The confirmation column remains untouched by both choices and exposes only this authored table's reuse gap.
The gap is not presented as expected selection bias or real generalization error.

datasets.name: procedural equal-margin paired-binary joint tables
datasets.split_definition: Two separate twenty-pair tables both fix candidate successes at 12 and baseline successes at 8; high-concordance cells are 8/4/0/8 and more-discordant cells are 4/8/4/4 in both-success/candidate-only/baseline-only/both-failure order.
datasets.unit_of_analysis: paired binary outcome for a named initial condition; each table is a separate authored negative control
leakage_controls: Both marginal success rates and the paired point difference are fixed before comparing joint tables.
All four joint cells and every pair identity remain recoverable.
The exact conditional calculation and its two-sided equal-tail convention are frozen before interpretation.
The diagnostic is explicitly barred from cluster, multiplicity, equivalence, effect-size, or safety claims.

protocol.comparison_unit: five authored row subfixtures (eight protocol episodes, ten paired outcomes in four routes, two separate twenty-pair joint tables, and four checkpoint score records) plus analytic zero-event bounds at three declared exposure counts and a ten-route-by-ten-replay pseudoreplication audit

randomness.rationale: Episode rows, paired route rows, both equal-margin joint tables, checkpoint score roles, suite membership, success rules, ten route identities, replay multiplicity, zero event labels, exact conditional convention, and exact cluster-resample enumeration are fixed.

protocol.action_space: not represented; the fixture begins from completed episode outcomes
protocol.timing: one completed episode is one analysis unit; no step frequency or wall-clock measurement exists
termination_conditions: Evaluate every valid row selected by the named protocol exactly once; at least one of terminated or truncated marks episode end, and both may be true on the same final step.
baselines: easy_goal_only protocol as an intentionally incomplete endpoint
baseline policy column in the paired route table
protocol.comparison_design: Cross easy/full populations with goal-only/safety-aware rules, then separately preserve candidate-baseline pairing within routes and compare episode-micro with equal-route-macro differences. Hold paired marginal rates fixed across two joint tables and compare their predeclared exact conditional diagnostics. The zero-event audit holds ten route identities fixed while varying repeats per route, and labels episode-event and new-route-incidence estimands separately. The checkpoint audit chooses on the selection column before reporting final, then contrasts this with deliberate final-set reuse and an untouched confirmation column. Do not interpret authored arithmetic, p-values, reuse gaps, four-cluster percentiles, or either zero-event bound as model ranking or population effects.
protocol.selection_protocol: All four protocol definitions, eight episode outcomes, ten route-cluster policy pairs, two twenty-pair joint tables, exact two-sided convention, four checkpoint rows, split roles, route identities, cluster membership, independent-unit declarations, and target estimands are fixed. Checkpoint selection may use only the selection column; final and confirmation columns never feed back into the legitimate choice. A valid truncated timeout stays in the denominator. A declared technical-invalid attempt aborts aggregation; any future retry, replacement, exclusion, test direction, cluster, multiplicity, correlation, or weighting policy must be frozen before execution.
protocol.failure_definition: goal-only counts goal completion; safety-aware additionally requires no collision and no intervention. A valid timeout without goal completion is a failure. Technical-invalid attempts are reported but never silently converted into failures or removed from a completed aggregate.

metrics.name: success_rate
metrics.split: reported separately for all four population-by-success-rule cells
metrics.aggregation: success count divided by the complete protocol-specific episode denominator

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: Two-sided Wilson score intervals show small-sample uncertainty under an explicit independent Bernoulli assumption; authored episodes may violate population-sampling assumptions.

metrics.name: collision_rate
metrics.split: reported separately for each protocol-selected episode set
metrics.aggregation: collision count divided by the complete protocol-specific episode denominator

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The smoke emits a deterministic point value only; it must not be used as a risk estimate.

metrics.name: intervention_rate
metrics.split: reported separately for each protocol-selected episode set
metrics.aggregation: intervention count divided by the complete protocol-specific episode denominator

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The authored fixture is not a sampled intervention-rate study.

metrics.name: mean_route_completion
metrics.split: reported separately for each protocol-selected episode set
metrics.aggregation: arithmetic mean route completion over the complete protocol-specific denominator

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: No population or repeated-seed interval is estimated by this fixture.

metrics.name: comparability_warning_count
metrics.aggregation: count distinct task-population, success-definition, and denominator mismatches

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: This is a deterministic contract audit count rather than a sampled metric.

metrics.name: episode_accounting_counts
metrics.split: reported as attempted, valid, terminated, truncated, and invalid counts per protocol
metrics.aggregation: count rows by predeclared validity and terminated/truncated flags before outcome aggregation; a simultaneous terminal and timeout contributes to both end-reason counts but only one attempted episode

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: These are deterministic provenance counts, not estimates from a sampled population.

metrics.name: protocol_interaction
metrics.aggregation: difference between the safety-rule contrast on full and easy populations; also report both conditional population contrasts and both conditional safety-rule contrasts

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: This is an exact arithmetic contrast on authored rows, not an estimated population interaction.

metrics.name: paired_cluster_success_difference
metrics.split: ten paired outcomes in four route clusters
metrics.aggregation: candidate minus baseline is computed within each pair; episode-micro weights every pair, while the target macro estimand averages four route-level mean differences equally

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The teaching fixture enumerates all 4^4 route resamples and reports a percentile interval for the equal-route macro difference; four authored clusters are far too few for a calibrated population claim.

metrics.name: zero_event_one_sided_upper_bound
metrics.split: zero observed events at 20, 100, and 1000 independent-trial exposures
metrics.aggregation: solve (1-p_upper)^n = 0.05 for the exact one-sided 95% binomial upper bound

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: Method is the exact one-sided binomial upper bound for zero observed events. The deterministic values expose why zero observed events do not imply zero risk; independent Bernoulli assumptions do not cover clustering, unseen hazards, scorer misses, or sim-to-real shift.

metrics.name: zero_event_pseudoreplication_audit
metrics.split: ten authored independent route clusters with one versus ten repeated members per cluster
metrics.aggregation: apply the zero-event bound once to the hypothetical independent-episode count and separately to the independent-cluster count while preserving different estimand labels

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: Both numbers are exact zero-event binomial bounds only under their declared independent units. They target different parameters and do not estimate within-cluster correlation, effective sample size, or real policy risk.

metrics.name: checkpoint_final_set_reuse_gap
metrics.split: four authored checkpoints with selection, final, and untouched confirmation roles
metrics.aggregation: select once by the selection score and report its final score; for the negative control, maximize the final score and subtract that checkpoint's untouched confirmation score

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The 0.25 gap is exact only for the authored score table. It illustrates role leakage and is not an estimator of expected selection bias or generalization error.

metrics.name: paired_margin_exact_conditional_diagnostic
metrics.split: two authored twenty-pair joint tables with identical candidate and baseline margins
metrics.aggregation: retain the four paired-binary joint cells; condition on b+c discordant pairs and double the smaller exact Binomial(b+c, 0.5) tail, capped at one

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: This field records no uncertainty interval: the reported values are equal-tail exact conditional two-sided McNemar p-value diagnostics for two authored tables. They provide neither an effect-size interval nor cluster, multiplicity, adaptivity, equivalence, or population-sampling inference.

distribution_shift.rationale: Easy versus hard suite membership is a protocol-population difference, not a calibrated OOD-score experiment.

disaggregations: paired 2x2 joint cell and discordant direction
zero-event bound by declared exposure count
checkpoint score by selection, final, and untouched confirmation role
reporting.raw_predictions: No model predictions exist; the complete eight-row protocol table, ten-row paired route table, two separate twenty-row equal-margin paired tables, four-row checkpoint score table, three analytic exposure counts, and ten-route-by-ten-replay authored counts are embedded in the source fixture.
reporting.failure_artifacts: Each failed, collided, or intervened episode remains as a named row in the fixture; there is no video.
confounders: The compared protocols use different task populations.
The compared protocols use different success definitions.
The compared protocols use different denominators.
Denominator change follows suite selection and is not an independent randomized factor.
Population and success-rule effects interact on the authored rows.
Unequal repeats across routes change the episode-micro estimand; the macro result instead weights each observed route equally.
Only four route clusters exist, so the enumerated percentile interval is a mechanics demonstration rather than calibrated inference.
The equal-margin tables are separate authored negative controls; their exact conditional values do not establish pair independence, an effect-size interval, equivalence, or multiplicity control.
The zero-event calculation treats exposures as independent Bernoulli trials and cannot cover correlated routes, unseen hazard types, scorer misses, or simulation shift.
The pseudoreplication audit contrasts different parameters; it does not estimate an intracluster correlation or convert ten routes into an effective per-episode sample size.
The checkpoint scores are authored to demonstrate split-role leakage; the 0.25 reuse gap is not an empirical estimate of expected selection bias.
Episode rows are authored and are not independent draws from a real deployment population.
No empirical reset, logging, or timeout failure rate is estimated.
reporting.missing_value_policy: All fields on all selected episode rows are required. Valid rows have no invalid reason; invalid rows require one and block aggregation. No row deletion, retry substitution, or imputation is allowed.

limitations: The eight protocol outcomes and ten paired route outcomes are hand-authored and do not measure any policy or environment.
The Wilson intervals assume independent Bernoulli trials and do not repair protocol incomparability; they are not applied to the clustered subfixture.
The factorial contrasts are exact for the authored table but are not population causal-effect estimates.
The exact 256-resample route bootstrap has only four authored clusters, uses a simple percentile interval, and is not calibrated population inference.

The two twenty-pair tables hold margins fixed but do not estimate a real paired effect; their exact conditional diagnostics omit effect intervals, clustering, multiplicity, adaptivity, and equivalence margins.
The ten-route pseudoreplication audit does not estimate correlation, effective sample size, route diversity, or either population event probability.
The four-checkpoint three-split table is a deterministic negative control and does not measure checkpoint quality, expected selection bias, or model generalization.
The fixture omits time-series logs, retries, real task sampling, video, exposure distance, and real safety events.
The invalid-attempt path is a contract test and does not estimate a real technical failure rate.
